questions.question: Which orbitals are filled in given order in 5^{ {th }} period of periodic table ?
questions.explanation: In the 5th period of the periodic table, the electrons fill orbitals in the following order: 5s (2 electrons) 4d (10 electrons) 5p (6 electrons) Total: 2 + 10 + 6 = 18 elements, matching the number of elements in the 5th period. Why other options are incorrect: B. 4s → 4d → 5d: 4s is filled earlier (in the 4th period), and 5d belongs to the 6th period. C. 4s → 5d → 4p: Incorrect sequence; 5d is not involved in the 5th period. D. 5s → 3d → 4p: 3d and 4p are filled in the 4th period. ✅ Correct Option: A. 5s → 4d → 5p

questions.question: If the atomic number of an element is 33 , it will be placed in the periodic table in the
questions.explanation: Let's determine the group of an element with atomic number 33. 1. Electronic configuration: The element with atomic number 33 is Arsenic (As). The electronic configuration of Arsenic is: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p3 2. Valence electrons and group: The valence electrons are in the outermost shell, which is the 4th shell. The valence configuration is 4s24p3. There are a total of 5 valence electrons (2 in 4s and 3 in 4p). For p-block elements, the group number is 10 + number of valence electrons. Therefore, the group number is 10 + 5 = 15. 3. Conclusion: Arsenic (atomic number 33) belongs to the 15th group (also known as the Nitrogen group or pnictogens). Therefore, the correct answer is 15th group.

hi.question: यदि किसी तत्व की परमाणु संख्या 33 है, तो यह आवर्त सारणी के किस वर्ग में स्थापित होगा।

questions.question: Which one of the following statements related to the modern periodic table is incorrect?
options: The p-block has 6 columns, because a maximum of 6 electrons can occupy all the orbitals in a p subshell
The d-block has 8 columns, because a maximum of 8 electrons can occupy all the orbitals in a d subshell
Each block contains a number of columns equal to the number of electrons that can occupy that subshell
The block indicates value of azimuthal quantum number (l) for the last subshell that received electrons in building up the electronic configuration
questions.explanation: The d-block has 10 columns (groups 3–12) because a d subshell holds up to 10 electrons, not 8; p-block’s 6 columns and block–azimuthal-quantum-number mapping are correct.

options: p-ब्लाॅक में 6 स्तंभ हैं, क्योंकि p-उपकोश में सभी कक्षकों को भरने के लिए अधिकतम 6 इलेक्ट्राॅनों की आवश्यकता होती है।
d ब्लाॅक में 8 स्तंभ हैं, क्योंकि d-उपकोश में सभी कक्षकों को भरने के लिए अधिकतम 8 इलेक्ट्राॅनों की आवश्यकता होती है।
प्रत्येक ब्लाॅक में स्तंभों की संख्या इस उपकोश में भरे जा सकने वाले इलेक्ट्राॅनों की संख्या के बराबर होती है।
ब्लॉक अंतिम कोश के लिए दिगंशी क्वांटम संख्या (l) को प्रदर्शित करती है जो इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास बनते समय इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करते है।

Na⁺: [Ne], Z=11 → cation → highest I.P. (hardest to remove electron) → Lowest I.P. in Series-I: N³⁻ Series-II: [N⁺, C⁺, O⁺] → Highest I.P. questions.question: Correct order of electronegativity of {N}, {P}, {C} and {Si} is
questions.explanation: Across a period EN rises (N > C), and down a group it falls (P < N, Si < C). Hence N > C > P > Si.

questions.question: Least electronegative element is
questions.explanation: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons in a bond. It decreases down a group and increases across a period. Caesium (Cs) is a Group 1 metal and lies at the bottom left of the periodic table — the region with the lowest electronegativity. Electronegativity order (approx): C (2.5) > Br (2.8) > I (2.5) >> Cs (0.7)

questions.question: The first ionisation potential of {Na} is 5.1 {~eV} . The value of electron gain enthalpy of {Na}^{+} will be

questions.explanation: Adding the first electron to oxygen is exothermic (∆H = –142 kJ mol–1) because neutral 0 atom accepts an electron easily. questions.question: Which of the following elements has highest electron affinity?
questions.explanation: Electron affinity is the amount of energy released when an atom in the gaseous state accepts an electron to form a negative ion. F (Fluorine) does have high electron affinity, but Cl (Chlorine) actually has a slightly higher electron affinity than fluorine. This may seem surprising, but it's due to electron-electron repulsions in the small 2p orbitals of fluorine. Chlorine’s 3p orbitals are larger and better accommodate the added electron. Approximate Electron Affinities (in kJ/mol): Na ≈ –53 K ≈ –48 F ≈ –328 Cl ≈ –349 (highest) Final Answer: C. Cl
